synthesis: Prime-supported square-free weights make the weighted GCD kernel large by rewarding shared divisors. The divisor-closed support carrying that gain is then compressed into short logarithmic clusters, with nearby squared weights aggregated into resonator coefficients. Because the smoothed moment sees logarithmic ratios rather than absolute integer sizes, clustered representatives retain the multiplicative relations to the resolution needed by the Fourier kernel. Expanding the zeta-resonator numerator gives a positive triple sum, so selected near-relations among representatives can be compared back to exact divisor relations in the original support and recover the GCD gain inside the moment ratio.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2278237719_v2_u02 states the large weighted GCD quadratic form and its role in constructing an essentially optimal resonator. Unit u04 constructs square-free multiplicative weights, rewrites the GCD objective through divisors, and factors its normalized gain into an Euler product on a divisor-closed support. Unit u09 groups that support in logarithmic intervals and defines the compressed coefficients used in the smoothed moments. Unit u13 expands the numerator into nonnegative Fourier terms, restricts to multiplicative coincidences, uses clustering and Cauchy-Schwarz to recover the divisor sum A_N, and divides by the normalization bound to prove the zeta extreme-value lower bound.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis follows one arithmetic object through two changes of representation: shared divisors become weighted GCD mass, logarithmic clustering turns that mass into frequency-resolved resonator coefficients, and positivity in the Fourier expansion turns selected frequencies back into the original divisor/GCD quantity. This explains why the arithmetic near-extremizer supplies analytic numerator gain.
limits: Clustering does not preserve every original ratio exactly; it preserves enough logarithmic resolution for the stated smoothing and comparison estimates. Positivity depends on the chosen positive coefficients and positive Fourier transform and is not automatic for arbitrary resonators or smoothers. The kernel normalization, prime weights, cluster windows, Fourier factors, triple-sum constraints, error terms, and nested-log exponent are heavily OCR- and formula-sensitive and require the PDF. The conclusion is a source-specific lower bound for large values of zeta on the stated interval, not a statement about zeta zeros, RH, exact extremizers, or a general arithmetic-to-spectral equivalence.
quality_reason: Accepted after replacing exact ratio preservation by preservation at the smoothing resolution. The four parents jointly support the complete mechanism from multiplicative overlap to a positive smoothed zeta-moment gain, which no parent supplies alone.

synthesis: The construction separates local gain from global capacity control. A finite band of primes defines square-free multiplicative weights whose local contributions factor into an Euler product; logarithmic expansion and prime-density integration establish its asymptotic gain. The full square-free support generated by that finite band is finite but potentially enormous, so blockwise prime-occupancy caps select a divisor-closed subset of size at most N. An exponential tilt proves that the discarded weighted tail is negligible, while a later complementary-divisor estimate shows that the retained support also loses negligible mass in the divisor range excluded by the resonator argument.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2278237719_v2_u04 defines the prime-local weights and Euler-product objective. Unit u05 linearizes that product and evaluates the prime sum at the required exponential scale. Unit u06 partitions eligible primes into blocks, caps occupancies, and proves that the remaining divisor-closed support has cardinality at most N. Unit u07 applies a b>1 tilt to the overload tails and obtains a negative exponent, proving negligible loss from the truncation. Unit u10 uses complementary divisors and a fractional-power penalty to remove a further large-ratio tail uniformly on the constructed support.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis couples a product-form reward with two different compression certificates: combinatorial occupancy bounds enforce finite capacity, exponential tilting preserves the main Euler-product mass, and complementary-divisor reindexing preserves the downstream portion needed by resonance. It thereby distinguishes support size, extremal mass, and resonance-compatible mass rather than treating compression as one unproved step.
limits: The eligible prime band is finite, so the premise is a very large finite support rather than an infinite one. The exponential tilt is a deterministic weighted-tail estimate, not a probabilistic theorem, and the complementary-divisor estimate is uniform only for the specially capped support. The paper constructs a nearly maximal family but neither identifies nor characterizes an exact extremizer. Prime intervals, floors, occupancy thresholds, binomial estimates, tilt exponents, fractional powers, Euler factors, and asymptotic uniformity are extraction-sensitive. No uniqueness, optimal support geometry, or transfer to unrelated kernels is established.
quality_reason: Accepted with the finite-support correction. The five parents jointly prove a concrete local-design/global-compression mechanism and separately justify cardinality control, preservation of the extremal main term, and preservation of the divisor mass needed downstream.

synthesis: The weighted GCD theorem supplies a large optimized quadratic form for every sufficiently large dimension. Defining Gamma(N) for the uniform GCD average and Lambda(N) for the optimized Rayleigh quotient gives Gamma(N)<=Lambda(N), while a cited reverse comparison controls Lambda(N) by a logarithmic factor times the running maximum of Gamma(n). Consequently the weighted gain cannot remain hidden at all uniform scales: it forces arbitrarily large unweighted configurations and shows that the exponent constant in the earlier general GCD upper bound cannot be taken below one.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2278237719_v2_u02 states the weighted lower bound with positive coefficients for every sufficiently large N. Unit u08 defines the weighted and unweighted extremal quantities, invokes their two comparison inequalities, combines the reverse comparison with Theorem 2, and derives Corollary 1 for arbitrarily large unweighted configurations; it explicitly says this makes the earlier upper bound fail when its exponent constant A is below one.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis uses the comparison inequality as a transfer principle from an optimized vector to a running maximum over uniform vectors. This converts a weighted asymptotic theorem into an unweighted obstruction while exposing the accompanying loss in quantifiers.
limits: The reverse comparison between Lambda and the running maximum of Gamma is cited from another work and not proved in the supplied unit. Exact normalizations, logarithmic factors, constants, maxima, and exponent scales are visually crowded and require PDF verification. The direct conclusion is a subsequence of arbitrarily large unweighted scales, not every sufficiently large N; the stronger statement requires monotonicity machinery that the authors explicitly omit. The result concerns GCD-sum upper-bound optimality and supplies no claim about zeta zeros or exact extremizers.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two parents jointly support a precise weighted-to-unweighted transfer and its optimality consequence, with the cited comparison and weakened quantifier stated rather than silently strengthened.

synthesis: The resonance proof keeps three burdens separate. An oscillatory estimate controls the excluded low-height interval by splitting near and separated logarithmic frequencies; Fourier decay and local cluster counting bound the denominator moment M_1; and a finite zeta approximation plus positivity reconstructs the GCD quantity inside the numerator M_2. These proved estimates make the moment ratio succeed. The concluding source remark then diagnoses, tentatively and only for this Soundararajan-style architecture, a remaining restriction from resonator-support capacity together with the available GCD upper bound, suggesting that the method can improve only the constant modestly.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2278237719_v2_u11 proves the low-height estimate by the minimum of interval length and inverse logarithmic frequency and a shell decomposition. Unit u12 bounds M_1 through the Gaussian Fourier transform, suppression of separated pairs, and control of nearby clusters. Unit u13 proves the positive numerator lower bound, recovers A_N, and completes the moment-ratio theorem. Unit u14 explicitly notes the repeated cardinality restriction on M' and, by reference to the crucial numerator estimate and GCD comparisons, says the method seems capable only of a slightly larger constant.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis is a proof-obligation ledger followed by a source-labeled bottleneck diagnosis: low-height removal, normalization cost, and positive gain are certified by different mechanisms, after which the authors trace the attainable constant backward through support capacity and the GCD input. It does not promote the final heuristic remark to a theorem.
limits: The low-height, M_1, and M_2 estimates are proved within their stated parameter choices, but the claim that the GCD bound is the active ceiling is an informed and tentative method diagnosis, signaled by the source's 'seems' language, not an impossibility theorem. Smoothing and truncation remain essential to the existing proof even if the concluding remark does not identify them as the ultimate scale barrier. A materially different resonator, smoother, support geometry, or proof architecture need not inherit this ceiling. Logarithmic frequencies, shell endpoints, Gaussian normalization, cluster windows, triple sums, errors, cardinality exponents, and constants are OCR-sensitive. No conjecture about the true maximal order of zeta is proved by the bottleneck discussion.
quality_reason: Accepted because the first three parents jointly establish a concrete separation of proof costs and gain, while the fourth provides an explicit but properly qualified architectural limitation. The result retains the exact distinction between theorem-level estimates and heuristic method diagnosis.
